XTIA SHAREHOLDER ACTION REMINDER: Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP Reminds XTI Aerospace Investors of Securities Class Action Lawsuit Deadline on October 27, 2026

XTIA SHAREHOLDER ACTION REMINDER: Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP Reminds XTI Aerospace Investors of Securities Class Action Lawsuit Deadline on October 27, 2026

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Oct. 17, 2026

Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP Securities Litigation Partner James (Josh) Wilson Encourages Investors Who Suffered Losses In XTI Aerospace To Contact Him Directly To Discuss Their Options

If you purchased or acquired securities in XTI Aerospace between April 15, 2026 and August 17, 2026 and would like to discuss your legal rights, call Faruqi & Faruqi partner Josh Wilson directly at 877-247-4292 or 212-983-9330 (Ext. 1310).

[You may also click here for additional information]

NEW YORK, Oct. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP, a leading national securities law firm, is investigating potential claims against XTI Aerospace, Inc. (""XTI Aerospace" or the "Company") (NASDAQ: XTIA) and reminds investors of the October 27, 2026 deadline to seek the role of lead plaintiff in a federal securities class action that has been filed against the Company.

Faruqi & Faruqi is a leading national securities law firm with offices in New York, Pennsylvania, California and Georgia. The firm has recovered hundreds of millions of dollars for investors since its founding in 1995. See www.faruqilaw.com.

As detailed below, the complaint alleges that the Company and its executives violated federal securities laws by making false and/or misleading statements and/or failing to disclose that: (1) that senior executives had engaged in certain undisclosed activities; (2) that these activities required Board review; (3) that there was reason to doubt the effectiveness of the Company's disclosure controls and procedures; (4) that, as a result, the Company would be unable to timely file its earnings reports; and (5) that, as a result of the foregoing, Defendants' positive statements about the Company's business, operations, and prospects were materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis.

On August 17, 2026, after the market closed, XTI Aerospace revealed that it could not timely file its Form 10-Q because it is "in the process of completing an internal review of the Registrant's former Chief Executive Officer, who resigned on August 17, 2026, and other related corporate governance matters." On this news, XTI Aerospace's stock price fell $0.25, or 15.9%, to close at $1.32 per share on August 18, 2026, on unusually heavy trading volume.

The court-appointed lead plaintiff is the investor with the largest financial interest in the relief sought by the class who is adequate and typical of class members who directs and oversees the litigation on behalf of the putative class. Any member of the putative class may move the Court to serve as lead plaintiff through counsel of their choice, or may choose to do nothing and remain an absent class member. Your ability to share in any recovery is not affected by the decision to serve as a lead plaintiff or not.

Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP also encourages anyone with information regarding XTI Aerospace's conduct to contact the firm, including whistleblowers, former employees, shareholders and others.

To learn more about the XTI Aerospace class action, go to www.faruqilaw.com/XTIA or call Faruqi & Faruqi partner Josh Wilson directly at 877-247-4292 or 212-983-9330 (Ext. 1310).

Follow us for updates on LinkedIn, on X, or on Facebook.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) for Investors Regarding the XTI Aerospace Securities Class Action Lawsuit:

What is the XTI Aerospace securities fraud lawsuit about?

Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP has filed a securities class action lawsuit against XTI Aerospace, Inc. (NASDAQ: XTIA) on behalf of investors who purchased shares during the Class Period. The complaint alleges that senior executives allegedly engaged in certain undisclosed activities that required Board review and that the Company's disclosure controls and procedures were allegedly ineffective. As a result, the lawsuit alleges, XTI Aerospace was unable to timely file its earnings reports, and Defendants' positive statements about the Company's business, operations, and prospects were allegedly materially misleading and/or lacked a reasonable basis. The alleged misconduct came to light on August 17, 2026, when XTI Aerospace disclosed after market close that it could not timely file its Form 10-Q due to an ongoing internal review of its former Chief Executive Officer, who resigned that same day, and related corporate governance matters. On this news, XTI Aerospace's stock price allegedly declined $0.25, or approximately 15.9%, to close at $1.32 per share on August 18, 2026, on unusually heavy trading volume.

Who may be eligible to participate in the lawsuit?

Investors who purchased or otherwise acquired XTI Aerospace, Inc. (NASDAQ: XTIA) shares on the NASDAQ exchange between April 15, 2026 and August 17, 2026, inclusive, may be eligible to participate in this class action lawsuit. Eligibility to participate is not limited to those who apply to serve as lead plaintiff; any class member who purchased shares during the Class Period may potentially share in any recovery obtained. Investors are encouraged to review their trading records to determine whether their purchases fall within the defined Class Period. Those with questions about their eligibility are encouraged to consult with counsel to evaluate their options.

What is a lead plaintiff, and how can I seek appointment?

A lead plaintiff is a court-appointed representative who acts on behalf of all class members in directing the litigation, including making key decisions about case strategy and settlement. Any investor who purchased XTI Aerospace shares during the Class Period may move the court for appointment as lead plaintiff, and the deadline to file such a motion is the lead plaintiff deadline in this matter. Courts generally appoint the movant with the largest financial interest in the case who otherwise satisfies applicable legal requirements as lead plaintiff. Importantly, investors are not required to seek appointment as lead plaintiff in order to be eligible to share in any recovery that may result from the lawsuit. Class members who do not serve as lead plaintiff may still participate in any settlement or judgment obtained on behalf of the class.

Why should investors contact Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP?

Faruqi & Faruqi, LLP has represented investors in securities litigation for decades and has recovered hundreds of millions of dollars for shareholders. Investors who purchased XTI Aerospace securities during the Class Period may contact the firm to discuss their legal rights, potential claims, and the lead plaintiff process at no cost or obligation.

Prior results do not guarantee or predict a similar outcome with respect to any future matter. We welcome the opportunity to discuss your particular case. All communications will be treated in a confidential manner.

data.title: Three Days to Go: Four Core Highlights of the 2026 iCAUR International User Summit
data.description:
• With just three days to go, the 2026 iCAUR International User Summit will feature four core highlights under the theme "Classic Never Fades | Make It Yours": brand launch, user co-creation, test-drive experience and ecosystem engagement.
  • The iCAUR V25 will make its official debut at the summit, joining the V23 and V27 to further enrich the V Series lineup.
  • The first iCAUR Customization Festival will kick off, featuring 20 customized vehicles and the launch of “User-centric Experience” global user ecosystem.
  • The V Series Test-Drive Camp, Ecosystem Showroom, AiMOGA robot, Robotaxi products and technologies will deliver a multi-dimensional immersive experience.

WUHU, China, Oct. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The 2026 iCAUR International User Summit will run from October 19 to 23. With just three days to go before the opening, Chery Group’s iCAUR has unveiled a slate of highlights under the theme "Classic Never Fades | Make It Yours," including the world premiere of the V25, the first iCAUR Customization Festival, the V Series Test-Drive Camp, and interactive tours of the Ecosystem Showroom. Global media and attendees will experience iCAUR's Future-Classic Design philosophy firsthand, see how V Series vehicles go beyond mobility to enrich everyday life, and gain deeper insights into the open ecosystem co-created by iCAUR and its global user community.


【Poster for 2026 iCAUR International User Summit】

Highlight One: World Premiere of the V25, A New Addition to the V Series Family

The iCAUR Global Brand & V25 World Premiere will be officially held on October 19. Positioned as an all-way SUV, the iCAUR V25 will make its global debut at the event, expanding the V Series lineup alongside the V23 and V27.

Built for both daily city commutes and outdoor adventures, the V25 embodies iCAUR’s latest Future-Classic Design language through its iconic boxy silhouette, near 1:1 width-to-height ratio and signature round headlamps. Backed by the i-AWD (Intelligent All-wheel Drive) and Golden REEV (Range-extended Electric Vehicle) systems, the vehicle confidently handles diverse road conditions, enabling seamless transitions between urban travel, long-distance trips and outdoor exploration. Boasting more than 20 ecosystem interfaces, a 1.8-tonne towing capacity and 6kW external discharge capability, it supports lifestyle scenarios such as camping, cycling and photography. Three official customized vehicles based on the V23, V25 and V27 will also be showcased together on site, demonstrating the wide-ranging lifestyle integration possibilities of the V Series.


【V25】

Highlight Two: Inaugural Customization Festival, Putting User Creativity on Stage

Beyond official customized vehicles, genuine user creativity will take the spotlight at the first iCAUR Customization Festival. Built around “Classic Never Fades | Make It Yours”, the venue is split into three experience zones: Custom Car, Urban Lifestyle and Outdoor Lifestyle. A collection of customized vehicles from across the globe spans off-road, camping and urban commuting use cases, visually demonstrating the V Series’ potential for expansion in styling, functionality and ecosystem connectivity. Attendees may cast votes for their favourite builds and winners may receive limited-edition stickers. Within the Custom Car zone, participants can try modular installations under professional guidance, learn how vehicle interfaces power various functions, and exchange ideas with fellow enthusiasts worldwide. The Urban and Outdoor Lifestyle Experience Zones host interactive activities including coffee tastings, graffiti creation and physical challenges, helping users discover new connections between vehicles and daily life aligned with personal interests.

On the occasion, the brand will launch the “User-centric Experience” global user ecosystem.

Supported by four foundational pillars — official iCAUR customized vehicles, the iCAUR Customization Festival, the iCAUR APP and iCAUR Club Connect — this framework embeds user experience and creativity into product and ecosystem development. Using vehicles as its medium, the iCAUR Customization Festival establishes a platform for global vehicle owners, customization enthusiasts and the brand to communicate and co-create, turning “Classic Never Fades | Make It Yours” into an ongoing collective journey where users participate in defining what constitutes a classic.


【Past iCAUR Customized Vehicle】

Highlight Three: V Series Test-Drive Camp — Hands-on Vehicle Trials

Product experience moves beyond static displays to real-world driving scenarios at the V Series Test-Drive Camp. Both the V25 and the V27 will be available for test drives across urban roads, undulating terrain and complex outdoor surfaces, allowing media and users to get behind the wheel and experience the two boxy SUVs firsthand, evaluating power response, handling stability, off-road capability and ride comfort.

A core focus of the experience is how the vehicles maintain stability and handle changing terrain. The all-new Swift Agile Handling Platform engineered by iCAUR features a native NEV (New Energy Vehicle) architecture. Built on a modular building-block concept, it enables flexible integration of powertrain, chassis, intelligent systems and cabin space to address differentiated mobility needs. The platform-dedicated i-AWD system dynamically adapts drive configurations to road conditions and apportions wheel torque with millisecond responsiveness, elevating off-road capability and handling performance on slippery surfaces, gravel tracks and steep gradients. Golden REEV achieves high-efficiency fuel-to-electricity conversion with a thermal efficiency of 44.5%. Behind the wheel across varied terrain, attendees will directly experience how i-AWD optimises power distribution and driving stability, while appreciating the near-BEV (Battery Electric Vehicle) driving refinement delivered by Golden REEV technology.

Highlight Four: Ecosystem Showroom and New Product Launch by AiMOGA Robot, Unlocking New Technological Potential

Beyond vehicles themselves, the iCAUR Ecosystem Showroom centres its design on “Classic Never Fades”. It houses three zones — Lifestyle Lab, Time Corridor and Creation Hub — crafting an immersive experience that stretches from design inspiration to real-world living scenarios. The pavilion features V23 and V27 customized vehicles, V27 design sketches, user creations and ecosystem product exhibits. Visitors can trace a vehicle’s journey from design sketch to finished product, and see how it adapts to diverse lifestyle scenarios via interfaces, accessories and user imagination. Zones including the Life Lab and Time Corridor respectively explore urban living, sensory experience and personalised creation, showcasing iCAUR’s design philosophy and how users can leave their own mark on their vehicles through customization and co-creation. Attendees can draw inspiration from diverse customization concepts and witness how Future-Classic Design continues to evolve through user innovation.

During the summit, the brand will also unveil new products and technologies related to the AiMOGA robot and Robotaxi, offering global users another perspective to explore the application of intelligent technologies.

In three days’ time, “Classic Never Fades | Make It Yours” will come to life — from a single new vehicle to a thriving user community; from individual customizations to a continuously connected global ecosystem. Through these four core highlights, this year’s iCAUR International User Summit turns “Classic Never Fades | Make It Yours” from a brand statement into a tangible, visible and inclusive shared practice.

data.title: It was another great week for the average stock as market leadership shifts away from tech
data.description:
By Christine Idzelis and Isabel Wang

The S&P 500's tech sector just had its worst week in a year and a half, while an equal-weighted version of the index cemented a second-straight weekly advance

The average stock in the S&P 500 just had a decent week, although a slump in tech masked that shine at the index level.

Investors aren't bailing on the stock market, despite an ugly selloff in technology names this week that helped to saddle the S&P 500 with its worst weekly showing in months.

The S&P 500 SPX lost almost 2% even as the majority of the index's stocks actually advanced on the week. Seventy percent of stocks in the index posted weekly gains while 30% fell, according to Dow Jones Market Data. That helped the equal-weighted version of the index XX:SP500EW cement a second-straight week in the green. When the dust had settled, the S&P 500 had cemented its worst weekly showing since June, Dow Jones Market Data showed.

Following a powerful but narrow tech-led rally, this week's action offered the latest indication that market leadership is shifting once again. While tech stocks and some industrial names tied to the artificial-intelligence build-out slumped this week, the average stock in the increasingly top-heavy S&P 500 made it through a difficult week largely unscathed.

Defensive and interest-rate-sensitive areas of the market moved sharply higher this week, as stocks that had lagged over the past two months shot upward. This has given hard-hit corners of the market a chance to shine.

"Given that there's growing concerns around the AI trade and volatility in spending these companies are doing, it just makes sense for investors to broaden their view a little bit and look for other opportunities," said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise Financial, in a phone interview Friday. "Now money is rotating out of tech into areas that had been really depressed."

Certainly, it helped that interest rates in the bond market saw a big pullback from recent highs, providing some broad relief to stocks.

The Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF RSP, a popular exchange-traded fund that equally weights stocks in the index, rose 0.5% this week. By contrast, the S&P 500 saw its biggest weekly percentage drop since June 26.

The big drag on the S&P 500 is its largest sector, information technology XX:SP500.45, which was pummeled this week with a 6.4% drop. That left the tech sector with its biggest weekly loss since April 2025, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Meanwhile, seven of the S&P 500's 11 sectors saw weekly gains, FactSet data showed.

"Nobody really wants to be out of the market," said Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, in a phone interview Friday. "If people were really genuinely concerned about the stock market right now, they'd be selling and not rushing to buy something else."

Among traditionally defensive areas of the stock market, the S&P 500's consumer-staples sector XX:SP500.30 surged 5% this week. Another defensive area, healthcare XX:SP500.35, had a big climb of 3.4%, while rate-sensitive stocks like materials XX:SP500.15 and utilities XX:SP500.55 also jumped sharply.

The decline in interest rates this week was significant, as the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield BX:TMUBMUSD10Y "backed off pretty dramatically," Saglimbene noted. The 10-year Treasury rate fell this week to 5.097% on Friday, locking in its biggest weekly pullback since February, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Bond yields move inversely with bond prices.

That's down from the 10-year rate's recent high of 5.31% on Oct. 5. Yields on 10-year and 30-year BX:TMUBMUSD30Y Treasurys have risen to their highest levels in decades this year.

"With some improvement on the rates front, people do feel it's safe to move some money back into rate-sensitive sectors like financials XX:SP500.40, industrials XX:SP500.20 and real estate XX:SP500.60," Sosnick said.

The yield on the 10-year Treasury dropped Thursday despite a hot reading on wholesale inflation from the producer-price index that same day, partly because "there was a bit of a flight-to-safety trade on top of it surrounding CoreWeave," Sosnick said - referring to the neocloud company (CRWV) whose stock tumbled this week on worries over its AI-related borrowing.

Tech had been the stock market's "safety trade," rising when Treasury yields were spiking in September, as investors appeared confident about the AI trade continuing to power higher despite higher rates, said Keith Lerner, CIO at Truist Wealth, by phone on Friday.

Last month, tech looked like "the only place in town," he noted, "while all these other areas were beat up." Now, it appears the tide has turned.

"Instead of a broad-based selloff across the board, you're just seeing a rotation from tech to everything else," Lerner said. "A rotational market is better than when money is broadly leaving the market."

-Christine Idzelis -Isabel Wang

data.title: JinkoSolar Unveils Tiger Neo 5.0 All-Black Residential Solar Module with 25.52% Efficiency
data.description:
JinkoSolar Unveils Tiger Neo 5.0 All-Black Residential Solar Module with 25.52% Efficiency

JinkoSolar Unveils Tiger Neo 5.0 All-Black Residential Solar Module with 25.52% Efficiency

PR Newswire

SHANGRAO, China, Oct. 17, 2026

SHANGRAO, China, Oct. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd. ("JinkoSolar" or the "Company") (NYSE: JKS), today unveiled Tiger Neo 5.0, an all-black residential solar module built on its all-new TAC technology. The first version to reach the market, an all-black 48-cell module, delivers a maximum power output of 510 W with a module efficiency of 25.52%. It was designed to redefine the upper limits of what a scenario-specific module can deliver in both appearance and efficiency for premium homes and other architecturally refined residences.

The module showcases a deeper, more uniform and more refined black appearance than conventional back-contact (BC) modules. Semiconductor-grade low- and high-temperature processes bring the power temperature coefficient down to -0.24%/℃, meaning stronger energy yield in high-temperature environments.

TAC technology combines the excellent carrier transport of TOPCon with the low-temperature processing and positive electrode passivation of HJT, pushing peak cell efficiency to 28%, approaching the theoretical limit of monocrystalline silicon cells. Together with a zero-gap cell layout and hidden-ribbon technology at module level, the module achieves an efficiency of 25.52%. Compared with conventional BC products, it delivers approximately 30 W more power, and a lower temperature coefficient. Its deeper, more premium black appearance blends seamlessly into residential rooftops— especially dark-colored ones — making it a standout in the residential module category for both power and aesthetics.

"Our vision for Tiger Neo 5.0 was to develop a panel tailored to premium residential rooftops. It pushes the boundaries of both performance and aesthetics with innovations in cell technology, passivation processes, structural design, module format and interconnections. With this launch, we aim to help move the industry toward solutions tailored to specific applications," said Charlie Cao, CEO of Jinko Solar Co., Ltd.

About JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.

JinkoSolar (NYSE: JKS) is a holding company combining clean energy industrial operations and strategic investment in emerging technologies. Its industrial foundation is a controlling interest in Jinko Solar Co., Ltd. (SSE: 688223), a global leader in clean energy technology. The Company makes disciplined strategic investments in renewable energy, advanced materials, artificial intelligence, commercial space and other frontier technologies, drawing on its industrial experience and its ability to identify emerging technologies and bring them to commercial scale.

Through Jinko Solar Co., Ltd., the Company distributes its solar products and sells its solutions and services to a diversified international utility, commercial and residential customer base in China, the United States, Japan, Germany, the United Kingdom, Chile, South Africa, India, Mexico, Brazil, the United Arab Emirates, Italy, Spain, France, Belgium, Netherlands, Poland, Austria, Switzerland, Greece and other countries and regions.

JinkoSolar has over 10 production facilities globally, over 20 overseas subsidiaries in Japan, South Korea, Vietnam, India, Turkey, Germany, Italy, Switzerland, the United States, Mexico, and other countries, and a global sales network with sales teams in China, the United States, Canada, Brazil, Chile, Mexico, Italy, Germany, Turkey, Spain, Japan, the United Arab Emirates, Netherlands, Vietnam and India, as of June 30, 2026.

What to do next: To join the FuelCell class action, go to  https://rosenlegal.com/cases/fuelcell-energy-inc/join or call Phillip Kim, Esq. toll-free at 866-767-3653 or email case@rosenlegal.com for information on the class action. A lead plaintiff is a representative party acting on behalf of other class members in directing the litigation.

Why Rosen Law: We encourage investors to select qualified counsel with a track record of success in leadership roles. Often, firms issuing notices do not have comparable experience, resources, or any meaningful peer recognition. Many of these firms do not actually handle securities class actions, but are merely middlemen that refer clients or partner with law firms that actually litigate the cases. Be wise in selecting counsel. The Rosen Law Firm represents investors throughout the globe, concentrating its practice in securities class actions and shareholder derivative litigation. Rosen Law Firm has achieved the largest ever securities class action settlement against a Chinese Company. Rosen Law Firm was Ranked No. 1 by ISS Securities Class Action Services for number of securities class action settlements in 2017. data.title: I'm 63 and diagnosed with lymphoma. Should I take my Social Security next year?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'My plan is to continue working as long as I'm able to do so and invest my Social Security benefits while I'm still earning a paycheck'

"It may remain stable, or it could progress, so for now, it's a wait-and-see situation." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I'd like your thoughts, please. I'll be turning 64 next January and have been thinking about starting my Social Security benefits then. I was diagnosed with lymphoma. It may remain stable, or it could progress, so for now, it's a wait-and-see situation. Am I overlooking anything or missing something important in considering this strategy? I'd appreciate any thoughts or advice.

My plan is to continue working as long as I can and invest my Social Security benefits while I'm still earning a paycheck. I understand there's a limit to how much you can earn before reaching full retirement age without affecting your benefits, and I believe I'd be earning around that limit.

When I'm 64

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'I feel like a loser': My stock portfolio is swinging wildly. Is it finally time to worry?

Given the uncertainty surrounding your diagnosis, it's smart to regularly evaluate your financial security.

Dear (Almost) 64,

I'm sorry you're dealing with such a serious diagnosis on top of what is already a tricky decision. Your plans are realistic and optimistic, which is a good combination. If you are the lower-earning spouse, I see no problem with taking your Social Security in 2027. There is one caveat: if you claim at 64, applying for disability benefits later may not be an option if your lymphoma progresses. Before you decide, ask Social Security or a financial adviser how claiming early would affect that.

Otherwise, here's the trade-off: If you live well into your 80s, delaying benefits will result in higher lifetime monthly payments. Because a survivor's benefit is based on the deceased spouse's claiming age, a delay by the higher earner also means a larger benefit for the surviving spouse. If your health deteriorates, claiming earlier means you will enjoy your benefits now. Given the uncertainty surrounding your diagnosis, it's smart to regularly evaluate your financial security.

The earnings test is a big issue. Before full retirement age, Social Security withholds $1 in benefits for every $2 you earn above the annual limit ($24,480 in 2026). You say that you are currently earning "around that limit," and you also write that you make a good living. If you earn well above it, most or all of your benefits could be withheld, leaving no checks to invest. Social Security recalculates your benefits at retirement age so that money withheld is not lost.

You'll also have to account for any taxes on your investments. The Internal Revenue Service calculates tax due on your Social Security based on your "combined income," which consists of your adjusted gross income, tax-exempt interest, and half of your annual Social Security benefits. So up to 50% or as much as 85% of your Social Security benefits may be subject to federal income tax. Stacking benefits on top of a good salary makes that more likely.

If you live well into your 80s, delaying benefits will result in higher lifetime monthly payments.

When you reach full retirement age (67 for you, given your age), the Social Security earnings test no longer applies, so working won't reduce your monthly benefit. And while your Social Security benefits may be taxable on your federal return, some states do not tax Social Security benefits. So, given that you are still working and earning a good income, I understand your idea of investing your checks.

For married couples filing jointly, Social Security benefits typically aren't taxable at the federal level if your combined annual income is $32,000 or less. Between $32,000 and $44,000, up to 50% of benefits may be taxable; above $44,000, up to 85% may be taxable. These thresholds apply to combined income. See the IRS's Social Security benefits guidance and use Box 5 of your SSA-1099 when preparing your tax return.

If you keep working and collect Social Security, being taxed on your Social Security can sting, given that you are already paying 6.2% of your wages toward Social Security, in addition to the 6.2% that your employer contributes. That's because it goes toward a collective fund so Americans who can no longer work and/or wish to retire have a source of income. A tax adviser would be best able to run through all the scenarios.

Predicting the math

Your Social Security benefit at 64 would be reduced by 20% compared with your FRA. So let's assume that your benefit at age 64 is $2,000 a month; your FRA benefit at 67 would be close to $2,500 per month. Delaying from 67 to 70 increases the retirement benefit by 24%, before cost-of-living adjustments (COLAs). If your investments had a hypothetical 10% annual return before inflation, investing your checks might look attractive.

Let's take two scenarios: one with a 10% return and another with a more modest 7% return. If you invested your $2,000-a-month Social Security at 64, you could accumulate a lot in contributions, growing to roughly $80,000 at 7% or $83,500 at 10%, before taxes and fees. The exact total depends on the timing of your deposits, compounding, taxes and fees. The market rarely runs smoothly, and some years see a negative return, so nothing is guaranteed.

Obviously, waiting to collect your Social Security until 67 or later provides no accumulated investment, but your benefit would be higher by about $500 a month for life. Without investing, that extra $500 takes about 12 years to make up the $72,000 head start, so the break-even is roughly 79. If you claim at 64 and invest the benefits, the break-even point versus waiting until age 67 depends on your benefit, returns, capital-gains taxes, dividends, and how long you live.

Without investing, it would take about 12 years to make up the $72,000 head start.

A few reminders about the rules of survivor benefits: A surviving spouse who has reached FRA can generally receive up to 100% of their deceased spouse's benefit. You or your husband would not ordinarily receive both full retirement benefits added together. Instead, the survivor generally receives their own benefit or an eligible survivor benefit, with the applicable rules determining the amount payable. This is important if you are the higher earner.

Your diagnosis raises two other points. First, claiming reduced retirement benefits early could leave you worse off. If you can no longer work, you may qualify for Social Security Disability Insurance, which pays your full retirement age benefit without reductions that come from claiming early. (Some lymphomas are on Social Security's Compassionate Allowances list.) Second, Medicare begins at 65, with the Part B premium deducted from your Social Security.

Even taking your diagnosis into account, I wouldn't count out a long life just yet. The 10-year survival rates for lymphoma vary based on whether it is Hodgkin lymphoma or non-Hodgkin lymphoma, as well as the stage, your age, and the subtype. Survival statistics are very general and only give a glimpse into lymphoma mortality rates. Your oncology team is best placed to discuss your situation, assuming you want to factor that into your decision-making.

So what should you do? The fact that you're asking the question suggests that you're inclined to take your benefits earlier and keep working. Compare your actual Social Security estimates at 64, 67, and 70, and check how the earnings test will impact you for the years you plan to claim. If you are the higher-earning spouse, you may wish to wait. If your husband is the higher-earning spouse, he may wish to wait before claiming to maximize survivor benefits.

It's also not an apples-to-apples comparison. A delayed benefit provides you with a guaranteed income for life that is also adjusted for inflation. Investment returns are, as we know, uncertain.

data.title: Fed interest-rate decision this month is a closer call than markets think
data.description:
By Greg Robb

Here are some of the arguments against a Fed rate hike - and why some economists disagree with them

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh speaks during a news conference last month after the Fed hiked interest rates for the first time in three years.

For weeks, investors and Federal Reserve watchers had been expecting the central bank to hold interest rates steady when it meets later this month. But fresh worries about inflation based on new data suggest officials aren't coming to the October meeting with a predetermined outcome.

Futures markets expect the Fed to hold rates steady in October, assigning only a 17% probability of an increase. But many economists think that the Fed meeting on Oct. 27-28 is a much closer call. Some see a good chance the Fed will raise rates.

"I think it's a 50-50 call," said Ethan Harris, former chief economist at BofA Securities, in an interview. Harris thinks the Fed should hike, but believes the committee has been "dovish" and may be reluctant to hike again so quickly.

The Fed hiked rates for the first time in three years in September, shifting away from a policy of slow rate cuts in 2024 and 2025 as inflation worries eased.

Fed officials characterized the increase at the time as part of a plan of limited hikes designed more to increase momentum in the process of bringing inflation down, rather than to combat a burst of inflation.

But September's inflation data, which came in higher than expected, changed the picture, and some economists think the Fed needs to move more quickly.

"I think October is a live meeting. We think the Fed will raise rates in October and December," said Matthew Martin, U.S. economist at Oxford Economics, in an interview with MarketWatch.

No preview from Warsh on what the Fed might do

Fed officials won't be speaking publicly until after the decision. In his last public comments before the Fed's blackout period, Chairman Kevin Warsh was neutral about monetary policy, saying he didn't like to prejudge meetings.

"I don't believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings that we have in the balance of this year," Warsh said on the sidelines of the IMF/World Bank annual meeting in Bangkok.

The Fed seems to be facing two distinct scenarios.

One, laid out in an interview by former Philadelphia Fed President Patrick Harker, would be for the Fed to hike rates quickly by a quarter point in October and December, and then pause to assess the inflation outlook.

The Fed wants to get interest rates up to where they are putting downward pressure on the economy. Right now, rates in the current range of 3.75% to 4% don't seem to be accomplishing that, Harker said on CNBC.

Another benefit of swiftly raising rates would be to buffer the Fed's credibility as inflation fighters, he added.

Carl Weinberg, chief economist at High Frequency Economics, wrote that he thinks the latest inflation data will prompt enough Fed policymakers to pivot to support the October and December option.

Martin, of Oxford Economics, said the September inflation data showed acceleration outside of energy prices, a worrying sign since goods outside of energy tend to be less volatile. Consumer prices rose 3.7% over the past 12 months, while the producer-price index showed wholesale inflation running at a 6.3% rate.

The second scenario for Fed officials would be to move more slowly in combating inflation by hiking only once every three months, with moves in December and March. This fits with the views expressed by many Fed officials who said before the latest inflation data that there was no urgency to hike.

Some economists think the Fed wants to hold rates steady in October because the central bank doesn't want to raise interest rates six days before the midterm elections on Nov. 3 and risk looking political.

Harris thinks the midterm concern is a small factor for the Fed. "There is no way to behave around the election that won't get criticism from somebody, and they will get pilloried by the president no matter what they do," he said.

Many economists said choosing between the two scenarios is a tough call for the central bank.

One benefit of a pause in October is that it will give the Fed more time to assess the data and determine how far to go, Aditya Bhave, head of U.S. economics research for BofA Global Research, wrote in a note to clients. The cost would be that the Fed risks falling behind the curve given the booming U.S. economy, he added.

Lindsey Piegza, chief economist for Stifel Financial, said an October hike would signal "an elevated level of concern" for inflation, creating an opening for the market to push rates higher and put more downward pressure on the economy. The more patient approach might make the public wonder if higher inflation is here to stay, she noted.

-Greg Robb

data.title: GAC Showcases Multiple Models at Canton Fair: Systemic Global Expansion as a Response to High‑Level Opening‑Up
data.description:
GAC Showcases Multiple Models at Canton Fair: Systemic Global Expansion as a Response to High‑Level Opening‑Up

GAC Showcases Multiple Models at Canton Fair: Systemic Global Expansion as a Response to High‑Level Opening‑Up

PR Newswire

GUANGZHOU, China, Oct. 17, 2026

GUANGZHOU, China, Oct. 17, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- On 15 October, the 140th China Import and Export Fair (Canton Fair) kicked off in Guangzhou. Dubbed "China's No.1 Exhibition" with a 70‑year history, it serves as a vital window for global merchants to understand China, and one of GAC's stages to connect with the world. For international buyers, GAC serves not only as a sourcing platform but as a trusted channel for experiencing Chinese automotive innovation and building long-term local partnerships. Having made its debut in 2012, GAC has participated in the fair 30 times to date. Together with the Canton Fair, it has witnessed the transformation of Made‑in‑China products into Chinese global brands.

This transformation is reflected in GAC's global expansion journey through a string of continuously refreshed sales figures. Overseas sales stood at 90,000 units in 2024, hit 130,000 units in 2025, and exceeded 197,000 units in January‑September 2026, representing a year‑on‑year surge of 138.9%. GAC is sprinting full steam ahead toward its annual target of 300,000 overseas units. GAC has accomplished a shift from "product export" to "system‑level global expansion".

At the GAC booth, XT80, AION i60 and AISTALAND GX7 showcased intelligent driving, three-electric systems and premium cabins. The energy-ecology zone featured DC ultra-fast charging piles, 7 kW smart home chargers, multi-in-one electric drive units and PV-Storage-Charging-Swapping Technology, addressing range anxiety. Opening day drew buyers from Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Europe, Latin America and Africa. At the Music & Cuisine Festival, GAC built three immersive spaces blending smart mobility, Cantonese cuisine, camping and sports. The XT80, AION N60, GAC S7 and AISTALAND GT7 served as lifestyle carriers, letting guests enjoy morning tea, global cuisines and intangible cultural heritage.

GAC will advance its ONE GAC 2.0 strategy, deepening localized operations and expanding its systematic global layout. As a tribute to the Canton Fair's 70th anniversary and a new business card for China's auto industry, GAC will help drive Chinese intelligent manufacturing onto the global stage.

For further information about GAC, please visit https://www.gacgroup.com/en or follow us on social media.
